_doc.what: Annotated sample for .bee/config.json — copy the sections you need; every key here is optional (missing keys fall back to safe defaults). JSON has no comments, so this _doc block is the documentation; bee ignores unknown top-level keys, but remove _doc from your real config to keep it lean.
_doc.hooks: Per-hook kill switches. All nine ship enabled; set one to false only to debug that hook. Names match the hook files: session-init, prompt-context, write-guard, model-guard, state-sync, chain-nudge, session-close, tools-logger, codex-subagent-audit.
_doc.guards: idle_gate=true blocks source edits when no bee work is active (phase idle / compounding-complete). Disable per-repo only if you accept unrouted edits: bee config set --key guards.idle_gate --value false. max_read_lines (default 800) caps how many lines a single inbound file read may pull before the read guard trims it.
_doc.commands: The host project's own lifecycle commands — record real runnable commands, not descriptions. The keys are setup, start and test. `test` is the ONE declared test command. `bee test` runs it on demand and CI runs it on every push — the one deterministic net. Each cap records its own proof line `<command> — <result> — <scope reason>`; `bee close` and `bee worktree merge` check that recorded proof and run nothing themselves. `commands.verify` was retired in 2.1.0 — a leftover one is ignored and onboarding warns on it; delete it and move its command to `test`. A project that deliberately runs no tests sets `test` to the exact sentinel string `"none"` instead of a real command — every gate above then reports itself disabled in one loud line rather than running (decision 55b951e1). Per-language recipes (node/go/rust/python/php): docs/config-reference.md.

gate_bypass.values: false | "normal" | "full" | "total" (legacy true = normal). Set via the bee-bypass-gate skill, not by hand.
gate_bypass.false: default — every gate stops for the human.
gate_bypass.normal: auto-approves Gates 1-2 for tiny/small/standard work; high-risk/hard-gate work, secret reads, and review-P1 still stop.
gate_bypass.full: also auto-approves high-risk/hard-gate Gates 1-2; only secret reads and a review P1 still stop.
gate_bypass.total: zero stops: every gate, secret reads, and review P1 findings auto-proceed. The loud session banner reminds you it is on.

models.what: Configured per runtime (claude | codex | pi) then role — the JOB a piece of work is (model-role-split D2/D3, store 06e49368/3c9d6262), never a cost tier. Any non-empty role name is legal; a name this table does not carry falls through to the next name the dispatch asks for and warns, it never refuses. The one silent case is `code` or `read` on a runtime whose models.<runtime> configures NEITHER of them — the pre-roles window, where falling through is the intended no-op; configuring either key closes it for that runtime, and the sibling you left out warns from then on. `ceiling` is never configured here — it is an escalation flag, always the session model, not a role name. A missing/null slot = prompt-budget (the marker alone carries the role; the subagent inherits the session model). A fresh `bee onboard` writes exactly `code`, `read`, `extraction` and `generation` — the two names below with no fall-through into `known_roles` (`code`, `read`) plus the historical tail every ordered role list ends with (`extraction`, `generation`). `review` and `advisor` are shown below purely to illustrate their slot shapes: onboarding deliberately does NOT publish either, because both already resolve with no config key at all — review falls through to generation's model, and advisor (no fall-through, decision 4faf1de9) reads unset as "off"; a published default would silently decide that product question for every new host. Copy `review`/`advisor` into your own config only if you want to override that behavior on purpose.

slot_shapes.string: "haiku" — plain model name; dispatches carry it as the model param (economics: effective_model_status=pinned on claude).
slot_shapes.object_cli: { "kind": "cli", "command": "...", "promptVia": "stdin" } — external CLI executor. GATHER-ONLY by design: cell execution against a cli-shaped slot is refused (cli_tier_gather_only); gathers/reviewers/advisors run through it with the prompt piped via stdin. See config-sample-cli-executors.json for full examples.
slot_shapes.object_herding: { "kind": "herding" } — routes EVERY purpose against this slot (cell, gather, reviewer, advisor, extraction) through `bee herding run` automatically; the old gather/review/advisor default-model fallback is gone (herding-tier D1-D6, widened by herding-review-slots D1) — the operator who sets this slot owns the pane cost for every purpose it serves. The agent that runs is the single global `herding.agent_command` below by default; add "agent": "<name>" (herd-registry D1/D2) to look that name up in herding.agents instead — an unknown name refuses, listing every registry key. Optional "fallback": "default" (herding-review-slots D3) re-dispatches a failed run (spawn failure, timeout, invalid result) through the runtime's own default model path for that slot instead of leaving the failure loud with the pane kept; example spelling: { "kind": "herding", "agent": "agy-flash", "fallback": "default" }. Not set in this sample — a repo without an `herding.agent_command` set up should leave every slot at a plain model name or null. Canonical doc: bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md.
slot_shapes.null: slot unset — prompt-budget tier; on codex-native transport the effective model is inherited-or-unknown (the dispatch log records the honest split).
slot_shapes.description_field: Any OBJECT-shaped slot may also carry "description": "<what this role is for>" — planner documentation only, never a selector: the session preamble's Roles line shows it beside the role name (clipped to 60 chars) so an agent knows when to assign the role, and resolution, the model guard, and dispatch prepare all ignore the field. A plain-string slot cannot carry one — spell it { "model": "sonnet", "description": "..." } instead. Live example on the `generation` slot below.

models.advisor: The AO3/AO13 consult identity required before Gate 2's execution component opens on high-risk work. Claude default: fable (the session-class model). Set null to skip the advisor line in worker prompts when no advisor resolves.
models.seat_roles: The eight SEAT roles — one per parallel advisor position, so a blind-lane run or a hat wave can put a DIFFERENT model in each seat instead of sharing the one `advisor` slot (lane-model-diversity D1). Lanes: lane-1, lane-2, lane-3. Hats: hat-facts-gaps, hat-risks, hat-value, hat-alternatives, hat-user-impact. They live in this same models.<runtime> table — no second config file. The constant of record is SEAT_ROLES in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/models.rs, and it is CLOSED: only those eight names. Fall-through (D2): a seat whose slot resolves NOTHING — key absent, null, or a shape the resolver reads as nothing — falls through to `advisor` on a `--kind advisor` dispatch rather than refusing, so an unconfigured seat keeps working exactly as before this table existed; every other kind keeps the ordinary role_not_configured refusal, and so does a name outside the eight (a typo like hat-risk never quietly borrows the advisor's model). The `[bee-tier: …]` marker names the RESOLVED role — `advisor` after a fall-through — and the dispatch log records the asked-for seat as `requested_role` (D4). There is no dispatch-time model flag: the model comes only from this table. The rows below are shown on `claude` as examples only; onboarding publishes NONE of them, because absent is what fall-through is for. Procedure home for both seats: skills/bee-hive/references/gates-and-delegation.md.
models.hat_description_rule: A configured `hat-*` slot states its purpose in `description`, so the table reads back self-documenting (lane-model-diversity D3) — which is why the hat rows below are object-shaped and the interchangeable `lane-*` rows are plain strings. The field stays DISPLAY-ONLY, exactly as `description_field` above says: resolution, the model guard and dispatch prepare all ignore it. So a string-shaped `"hat-risks": "opus"` resolves perfectly well; `bee doctor` merely reports it as an unlabelled hat — an advisory line, never a verdict, never a refusal. A `null` hat is a seat switched OFF, not an undescribed one, and is passed over.
models.codex_note: On codex-cli 0.144.4 native subagents cannot pin a per-agent model — a string here records the REQUESTED model; the dispatch log will still say effective_model_status=inherited-or-unknown until a capability probe proves per-agent selection.
models.pi_note: RESULT DELIVERY (pi-result-mailbox D1/D2/D6): a Pi worker's result digest DOES return. The PRIMARY contract is the synchronous one every runtime shares — `bee herding run` blocks and prints the validated result envelope, which carries `report_path` (a path, never the report body at any size) whenever the worker wrote its `report-N.md`, and `report_note` when a report was expected but is missing or stale. Both keys are ADDITIVE: a result with no report keeps the exact envelope key set it had before this feature. Async delivery is Pi-only and OPT-IN — `bee herding run --inbox-session <orchestrator-session-token>` IS the detached fact: it writes a pending marker under `.bee/result-inbox/<token>/` before the pane spawns, and the checked-in `.pi/extensions/bee-guard.ts` drain injects the finished job's HEADER ONLY (job_id, cell_id, status, summary, proof, report_path) into that session — steered when the session is busy, a fresh turn when it is idle. Know the limits before you lean on the async half: delivery is AT-LEAST-ONCE, so the injected job_id is the DEDUPE KEY and a job_id already handled in that session is a replay, not a second result; the drain runs only inside a LIVE Pi session, so a job finishing while no session is up waits in its marker until one starts; the report BODY never rides an injection (read report_path yourself); and one dispatch takes exactly ONE path — a run with no `--inbox-session` writes no marker and is read from its own output. THE LAW (pi-support D5): models.pi is a HERDING-ONLY door. `bee dispatch prepare --runtime pi` and `bee dispatch wave --runtime pi` resolve this table in the one config home every other runtime reads, and EVERY slot must resolve {"kind":"herding"} (optionally with "agent": "<herding.agents name>"). Pi ships no Agent/subagent tool surface (store 7f9c8518), so any other payload would dispatch NOTHING while the envelope read as a successful dispatch — therefore a plain-string model, {"kind":"native"}, {"kind":"cli"}, a null (prompt-budget) slot, and an escalated cell (session model, `bee cells escalate` or `--role ceiling`) are each refused BY NAME with reason "pi_requires_herding", naming the slot, the resolution word (model | native | cli | budget | escalation) and its fix. The escalation refusal carries its own remedy: Pi has no subagent surface — run the escalated cell inline in the session. Seat roles (lane-*, hat-*) ride along under the same law, and an unconfigured seat still falls through to `advisor` — which is why the advisor slot below is herding too. THE VALUES (pi-support D6, the settled table): heavy roles (code, test, docs, review) run a herding agent that is `claude --model opus`; advisor is `claude --model fable`; cheap roles (read, extraction, generation, supervisor) run agy-flash. Herding constrains the TRANSPORT, not the model vendor. Canonical doc: docs/config-reference.md.

retry.what: `retry.fallbackChains` — the RUNTIME fallback chain (model-role-split D10/D11, store 50808d48). A map: key = a role name, a concrete model selector, or a "provider/*" wildcard; value = an ordered list of model selectors to try after a failure. Distinct from the resolution fall-through under `models` above: fall-through answers an UNCONFIGURED name before anything runs; a chain answers a model that was reached and FAILED.
retry.explicit_only: There is NO built-in chain for any role and no role inherits one — a `default` key is refused out loud (decision 4faf1de9's advisor, which records a walled consult as NOT OBTAINED rather than substituting a lesser model, must not change because someone else configured a chain). No `retry` key is set in this sample on purpose: with none configured every dispatch payload is byte-identical to a bee that had never heard of chains, and a chain only exists because you typed it.
retry.example: "retry": { "fallbackChains": { "code": ["sonnet", "haiku"], "opus": ["sonnet"], "anthropic/*": ["local/qwen"] } } — a role-keyed chain, a model-keyed chain that follows that model into whatever role is assigned it, and a provider-wide chain. Most specific key wins: concrete model, then "provider/*", then role.
retry.what_bee_publishes: bee does not execute dispatches, so it never runs a chain (decision 51341f84). `bee dispatch prepare` RESOLVES the chain for this dispatch and publishes it on the payload beside the model as `fallback_chain: {key, chain, fallback_when, advance_on, never_advance_on}`; advancing a step, and recording the step taken, belong to whoever executes the payload. A dispatch that names no model (escalated/session-model, cli-exec, herding pane) carries no chain — there is nothing to fall from.
retry.the_gate: A step may fire ONLY on a transient or infrastructural failure — advance_on: quota_or_rate_limit, provider_auth_or_policy_rejection, empty_response, malformed_tool_call_replay_safe, stream_stall_or_connection_reset, server_error_5xx. A step may NEVER fire on a semantic failure — never_advance_on: tool_error, wrong_or_unwanted_result, failed_proof, red_test. A red test moving the work to another model would hide the defect; the chain absorbs the provider, never the result.
retry.validation: Junk drops with a warning on stderr rather than half-reaching a payload: a non-array chain, an empty chain, whitespace-only steps, duplicate steps (first wins) and a step naming the key's own model are all ignored.

_doc.dogfood_repos: Only used in bee's own source repo (self-improvement loops); host projects can omit or leave [].
_doc.product_root: Optional, for the workshop+nested-product topology only: where the product's own docs live when they are NOT beside .bee/ (path relative to the bee root, or absolute). Unset = the bee root; do not set it speculatively — a set-but-missing path warns loudly on every read.
_doc.cells_archive_on_close: true (default) lets a green `bee close` retire the feature's capped cells into .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/, out of the path status/orient parse on every call. Set false only if your own tooling reads .bee/cells/*.json by path; reverse with bee cells unarchive --feature <f>.
_doc.ship_visibility: How finished work is surfaced: "off" (default) or "draft-pr". An unrecognized value normalizes to "off" and says so once, by name.
_doc.worktree_first: Code-touching feature work lives in its own worktree; the write guard refuses feature edits made in the main checkout. Set to the exact string "off" to disable that refusal for a repo that deliberately works in main.
_doc.worktree_cleanup_on_merge: true (default) lets `bee worktree merge` remove the worktree directory, delete its branch, and drop its grant automatically on a merge that merged something (opt one merge out with --no-cleanup). Set false to opt the whole repo out; a non-boolean value here is refused, never silently read as either outcome.
_doc.uat_stop: "close" (default, i.e. absent) lets `bee worktree merge` land the merge on main untouched, and moves the `uat` gate door to `bee close` instead — the product is testable on main, and the worktree is HELD (`--cleanup`/`worktree_cleanup_on_merge: true` ignored) while `uat` is pending. "merge" makes `bee worktree merge` itself enforce the `uat` gate for standard/high-risk features, exactly as `uat_before_merge: true` did. "off" removes the stop everywhere. Any other value refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_CONFIG_INVALID rather than guessing. `uat_before_merge` below is now read only as this key's back-compat alias.
_doc.uat_before_merge: Back-compat alias for `uat_stop`, read only when `uat_stop` is absent: true reads as "merge", false reads as "off" — but with BOTH keys absent, the default is now "close" (not this alias's own true/false shape). A non-boolean value here refuses WORKTREE_MERGE_UAT_CONFIG_INVALID rather than guessing.
_doc.staging_before_merge: false (default, i.e. absent) keeps the staging mixing ground off — staging is opt-in. Set true to turn it on repo-wide so `bee staging add`/`bee staging rebuild` work; leaving it absent or false makes both refuse STAGING_DISABLED, so the repo runs feature worktree -> uat gate -> main with no staging step. A non-boolean value here refuses STAGING_CONFIG_INVALID. Independent of uat_before_merge — the uat gate itself is unaffected.
_doc.doc_viewer: Opt-in URL prefix for a local doc viewer (e.g. mdview). base_url + project join as <base_url>/p/<project>/<repo-relative-path>, injected into the session preamble and the compaction capsule so agent prose links docs as URLs instead of bare paths. Unset = today's bare paths, silently. A half-set key (one field missing or empty, or a wrong-shaped value) produces no URL plus one stderr line naming the key. bee joins the URL, it does not encode it — a path containing a space needs percent-escaping by whoever writes the link.
_doc.herding: Runtime adapter for `bee herding run` / `--continue` (one external agent as a cell-execution worker, mailbox protocol, cell-only — the write-work mirror of the gather-only cli tier), `bee herding wave`, and `bee herding control-loop`. agent_command: the DEFAULT worker when no herd name is given — either a JSON array of argv tokens, or (shown live below) a plain STRING naming a herding.agents entry so the command is written exactly once. Array form: JSON array of argv tokens for the WORKING agent — token 0 is the herdr agent kind (21 kinds), passed straight through to herdr with no bee-side allow-list; the rest is the agent's own argv. Default when absent: ["claude", "--model", "sonnet", "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions"]. control_command: the control pane's real invocation inside bee herding control-loop, with {PROMPT}/{MODEL}/{MAX_TURNS}/{ALLOWED_TOOLS} placeholders. agents (herd-registry D1, optional): a map, name -> argv token array, same shape and per-entry validation as agent_command; a malformed entry is dropped, fail-open, never poisoning the rest. Example (set live below: claude-sonnet, claude-opus, claude-fable and agy-flash — the last three are what the models.pi table above names, since the pi runtime dispatches ONLY through herding; the registry is inert until referenced, safe in every repo). Another shape: {"agents": {"gemini-generation": ["gemini", "--yolo"], "codex-review": ["codex", "exec", "--model", "{MODEL}"]}} — three reference spellings resolve a name against it (herd-registry D2): a tier slot's {kind:herding, agent:<name>}, `bee herding run --agent <name>`, and a plain-string agent_command naming a herd; an unknown name refuses, listing every registry key. An entry may instead be an object {"argv": [...], "env": {...}, "workspace_trust": {...}} (per-agent env export, plus (herding-prompt-stall D5, set live below on agy-flash) a workspace-trust declaration: "file" (a foreign tool's own trust-store JSON file, leading ~ expanded) and "key" (the array field inside it holding trusted absolute paths) — before the pane split, bee reads that file and appends the run's --cwd when absent, so a herd agent that gates on a per-workspace trust prompt never meets it in a freshly minted worktree; every failure mode (missing file, bad JSON, missing/non-array key, unwritable file) warns and lets the run proceed, fail-open, and a malformed workspace_trust drops the whole entry like a bad env key does. All keys optional and independent. Canonical doc: bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md. OPERATIONAL RULES (live-proven 2026-08-20): the spawn survives a booting shell (agent start retries agent_pane_busy up to 10 times ~1s apart); the brief is never typed into the pane — it is written to <mailbox>/brief-N.txt and the agent receives a one-line pointer, submitted once through herdr's own observed submit; the receipt is the worker's ack file (or the round result), and a resend fires only when the agent returns to ready with no ack; a run that fails keeps its pane as forensics, a run that succeeds closes it. Put each kind's auto-approve flag in its herd entry (claude: --permission-mode bypassPermissions; agy: --dangerously-skip-permissions) — a pane sitting on a question is named in the give-up message. NEVER type into a live worker pane: a human keystroke hijacks the agent's turn and the brief goes unanswered. TRANSPORT (tmux-herding-transport D1-D4, widened to the whole cockpit by tmux-herding-cockpit D1): transport picks which terminal multiplexer bee reaches a worker pane through — "herdr" (default when absent, needs the herdr binary on PATH) or "tmux" (needs tmux on PATH); bee never auto-detects it from $TMUX or $HERDR_ENV, and any other value refuses `bee herding run` before the job file, the mailbox, or any pane split. On tmux a worker is a pane split inside the CALLER's current tmux window under the same column rule and split lock — never a detached session — and the mailbox, control loop, merge gesture and every safety boundary are unchanged. tmux (all optional, all fail-open to the default on a malformed value): the screen-read knobs, held as DATA because marker strings are another tool's UI chrome and rot with its releases. busy_markers (default ["esc to interrupt", "esc to cancel", "ctrl+c to interrupt", "press esc to"]) in the last 2 non-empty screen lines means mid-turn; blocked_markers (default ["do you trust", "trust the files", "paste your api key", "press enter to submit"]) in the last 12 non-empty lines means a human must answer a dialog — the wait ends as blocked, the pane STAYS OPEN, and bee types nothing into it (D3); scrollback (default 40) lines per capture-pane read; quiet_cycles (default 3) identical reads that count as a settled screen; interval_ms (default 2000) delay between polls. A list override REPLACES the default list (an empty array means never classify on it). The screen verdict is ADVISORY ONLY (D4) — result-N.json and ack-N.json stay the only truth for done and delivered. Defaults come from upstream (D5: https://github.com/luongnv89/skills @ ab46724e, skills/tmux-agent-comms/). COCKPIT (tmux-herding-cockpit D1-D5): the same key — and NO new key — now selects the transport for the WHOLE cockpit, not for bee herding run alone. Occupancy crosses the wave ledger against tmux list-panes -a instead of herdr pane list, same fail-closed fallback; waves build fleet::backend::tmux::TmuxBackend beside the herdr one; the control pane's enumerated allowlist substitutes exactly ONE entry, Bash(herdr:*) becoming Bash(tmux:*), nothing else added or removed; bootstrap-cockpit.sh and the dispatch/merge role documents speak ONLY transport-neutral bee verbs (D2) — bee herding pane <current|list|split|run|send-text|read|rename|close|layout|tab-create|tab-list|tab-focus>, bee herding agent-start, bee herding pane-id --label, bee herding result — each printing one {ok, transport, result} envelope identical on both transports. tmux mapping (D3): workspace = the caller's current tmux session, tab = a window (cockpit, runtime), pane label = the pane TITLE (select-pane -T), chat pane = the pane bootstrap ran from, and label lookup reads list-panes pane_title. ONE screen classifier serves both crates (D4): it lives in fleet::screen and bee's RealTmux reuses it, with TmuxSettings::from_config resolving herding.tmux.* and handing the settings in — fleet never reads .bee/config.json itself. The pane-verb pre-send guard fails OPEN on an unreadable screen (D5) — an unreadable capture does not block the send — but a screen that classifies blocked always refuses.
